Present in milk; consider alternative or monitor

summary: Amlodipine is a long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that relaxes vascular smooth muscle, lowering peripheral resistance and blood pressure and improving coronary blood flow. It is indicated for hypertension and for chronic stable and vasospastic angina. The usual adult dose is 5 mg once daily up to 10 mg/day; lower starting doses are used in the elderly and in hepatic impairment. Peripheral edema is the most common dose-related side effect.
indications: Hypertension, alone or combined with other antihypertensives
Angiographically documented coronary artery disease to reduce risk of hospitalization for angina and coronary revascularization

dosage.d: Initial 5 mg once daily; maximum 10 mg once daily

dosage.n: Doses >5 mg not studied in children

dosage.d: Start 2.5 mg once daily; titrate slowly

admin: Take orally once daily at about the same time each day
May be taken with or without food
Titrate at intervals of 7-14 days based on blood-pressure or angina response
Do not stop abruptly in angina patients without medical advice
moa: Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium antagonist that inhibits the transmembrane influx of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle through L-type calcium channels, with selectivity for vascular smooth muscle. The resulting arterial vasodilation lowers peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure; in angina it dilates coronary arteries/arterioles and reduces afterload and myocardial oxygen demand.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to amlodipine or other dihydropyridines
relative: Recent acute myocardial infarction with unstable hemodynamics

preg: Limited data; amlodipine has been used in pregnancy-related hypertension. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Amlodipine is present in human milk with an estimated low relative infant dose. Consider the benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential effects on the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in renal impairment; amlodipine is extensively metabolized to inactive metabolites and is not dialyzable.
hepatic: Amlodipine is extensively metabolized by the liver, and clearance is reduced in hepatic impairment. Initiate at 2.5 mg once daily and titrate slowly with close monitoring.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole, ritonavir) - increased amlodipine exposure and hypotension
Simvastatin - limit simvastatin to 20 mg/day due to increased myopathy risk
moderate: Sildenafil and other PDE5 inhibitors - additive hypotension
minor: Grapefruit juice - modest increase in exposure
Dantrolene IV - theoretical risk of hyperkalemia/myocardial depression
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; grapefruit juice can modestly raise levels.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may add to the blood-pressure-lowering effect and dizziness.

serious: Worsening angina or myocardial infarction on initiation/up-titration (rare)
emergency: Acute pulmonary edema (in severe aortic stenosis)

monitoring: Blood pressure at baseline and after each dose change
Heart rate and symptoms of angina
Liver enzymes if symptoms suggest hepatic involvement
counsel: Take once daily at the same time each day, with or without food
Ankle swelling is common and dose-related; report if bothersome
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to limit dizziness
Do not stop suddenly if you have angina; contact your doctor
Report chest pain, fainting or marked swelling
pk: Store at 20-25 C; protect from light
pearls: Long half-life gives smooth 24-hour control and forgiveness for an occasional missed dose
Peripheral edema is dose-dependent vasodilatory, not fluid overload, and responds poorly to diuretics
Does not significantly depress cardiac conduction (unlike verapamil/diltiazem)
Limit simvastatin to 20 mg/day when co-prescribed
missed: Take the missed dose when you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one as scheduled; do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose can cause marked and prolonged peripheral vasodilation with hypotension and reflex tachycardia. Treat with active cardiovascular support: elevate limbs, give IV fluids, vasopressors and intravenous calcium; consider this agent's long half-life when planning duration of support. Dialysis is not beneficial as amlodipine is highly protein bound.
